standard.title: Interior Angle Sums
standard.description: demonstrate that the interior angle sum of a triangle in the plane is 180° and apply this to determine the interior angle sum of other shapes and the size of unknown angles
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify angle relationships on straight lines and at points (from AC9M6M04). Students understand that angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students demonstrate that the interior angle sum of a triangle is 180° and apply this and the decomposition principle to find interior angle sums of polygons and unknown angles.

nodes.label: Demonstrating the triangle angle sum
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students demonstrate, using concrete or dynamic methods, that the interior angles of any triangle sum to 180°.
nodes.minimum_width: Tear off the corners of a triangle and arrange them on a straight line to show they sum to 180°; verify with measurement for two different triangles.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate using paper tearing and using dynamic geometry software; explain why the property holds for any triangle.
wider: Investigate what happens to the angle sum if you draw a triangle on a sphere — explore non-Euclidean geometry informally.
Use the parallel lines result from AC9M7M04 to prove why the angle sum is 180° (formal derivation).

response_modes.reason: Students who only see one demonstration believe the angle sum might be different for unusual triangles. Testing acute, obtuse, right-angled, and very flat triangles builds confidence in the universality of the property.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who don't believe the 180° sum is universal make errors in Node 2 decomposition — if they think obtuse triangles have a different angle sum, the formula (n-2) × 180° breaks down and polygon calculations become unreliable.
success_criteria: Demonstrates the angle sum of a triangle is 180° using at least one method.
States the property applies to all triangles.
Measures angles in a triangle and verifies the sum is approximately 180°.

nodes.label: Interior angle sum of polygons by decomposition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students use decomposition of polygons into triangles to determine the interior angle sum formula for n-sided polygons.
nodes.minimum_width: Decompose a quadrilateral and pentagon into triangles and calculate their interior angle sums.
nodes.typical_width: Derive and apply the formula (n−2) × 180° for any polygon; verify for specific cases.
wider: Investigate the exterior angle sum of polygons (always 360° for convex polygons) — connect to interior angle sum.
Apply to regular polygons: find the interior angle of a regular hexagon, octagon — connection to tessellation.

response_modes.reason: Decomposition requires a systematic approach: draw diagonals from one vertex, count triangles, multiply by 180°. Students who decompose randomly get inconsistent results.

success_criteria: Correctly decomposes a polygon into triangles and calculates the interior angle sum.
States the general formula (n−2) × 180° and applies it correctly.
Can verify their result by measuring.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The generalisation to n-sided polygons and the exterior angle sum offer advancing students structural pattern recognition — connecting decomposition to a general formula is a rich algebraic-geometric link.

nodes.label: Finding unknown angles using angle sums
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students use triangle and polygon angle sum properties to find unknown angles, giving reasons.
nodes.minimum_width: Find an unknown angle in a triangle or quadrilateral using the angle sum property.
nodes.typical_width: Solve multi-step problems combining angle sum, straight line, and parallel line properties; give geometric reasons.
wider: Solve problems involving isosceles triangles where the angle sum property combines with the equal base angles property.
Design angle puzzles for peers — create a figure with multiple unknown angles that can be found step by step.

response_modes.reason: Finding unknown angles requires students to select and apply the right angle property from their repertoire simultaneously — a genuine integration of angle sum, supplementary, and parallel line results.

success_criteria: Correctly finds unknown angles using angle sum properties.
States the property used as the reason for each step.
Applies the correct angle sum for the polygon type.
